Most businesses are just looking to make a simple client scripts. Here's are hours, photos, menu, words about what we do/sell. Besides the occasional "Contact Us" text box which typically just sends an email, the websites are very simple.

To create a website that accepts content, you need server side scripting and a database. Server side scripting requires a server stack like LAMP, although many times you can't find hosted environments that remove the necessity of the backend, but you still have to be able to interact with the server through .yaml files or whatever method that particular stack requires.

Server side programming is a very different animal than client side programming like JavaScript. Databases themselves are on a whole different level. Attempting to build a database without understanding the concepts can create a clusterfuck of a database.

If you want to get into creating advanced websites that stores and manages user data, you would need to start by choosing a programming language and database and just hunker down and get to work going through those tutorials. I'd say if you put in about 40 hours a week for about 2 years you might be ready to start the process of creating a community-based website.

When you are ready, find some open source software designed for online forums and try to modify their software. It will help you understand all the gotcha's when creating something so complicated. There are a shit ton of variables to consider and one person working alone would take far to long and have to many costly mistakes, better to cut your teeth learning from those who have been developing similar software for many years.
